source.title: Safety at Scale: A Comprehensive Survey of Large Model Safety

approved.name: HarmBench
approved.size: 18 red-teaming methods / 33 target LLMs and defenses
approved.sourceEvidence: The LLM chapter names HarmBench as an evaluation benchmark. The official repository calls it a standardized evaluation framework and documents its evaluation pipeline.

approved.name: BUMBLE
approved.sourceEvidence: The LLM chapter explicitly calls BUMBLE a benchmark. The primary paper reports 12.7K instances across nine bias types, and the authors' repository identifies itself as the BUMBLE benchmark.

approved.name: JailbreakBench
approved.sourceEvidence: The LLM chapter names JailbreakBench. Its official repository calls it an open robustness benchmark and releases the JBB-Behaviors evaluation data, evaluation framework, artifacts, and leaderboard.

excluded.reason: The official JailbreakBench repository defines this as the evaluation dataset inside JailbreakBench, so it is represented as a resource link rather than a duplicate benchmark card.

These are auxiliary general-capability or preference-evaluation resources used by papers in the chapter; the audited source lines do not establish them as safety benchmarks introduced or curated by those papers.
The chapter uses COCO as a dataset; it is not identified there as an LLM safety benchmark.

The team-approved site domains remain LLMs, Agents, and Embodied AI. Candidate names from these four Safety at Scale chapters are retained in the audit output but are not published under an invented domain mapping.
